author: @TheSenRec
title: DAR chapter to hear from veteran advocate
text:
The John Percifull Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution will hear from the founder of a nonprofit focused on preventing veteran suicide during its meeting at 11 a.m. Thursday at the Garland County Library, a news release said.
Jared Eakin, founder and executive director of Scars and Stripes Inc., will be the featured speaker. The organization works to prevent veteran suicide through early intervention, housing assistance and other support services.
Eakin is a disabled U.S. Army veteran who later worked in the private sector in counterterrorism. After leaving the military, he faced challenges adjusting to civilian life, the release said, including untreated mental health issues.
Those experiences led Eakin to study social work and begin a career in behavioral health. He worked for several years as a substance abuse counselor before moving into services focused on veterans.
Eakin later worked as a Department of Veterans Affairs contractor with the Supportive Services for Veteran Families program. He assisted homeless veterans across Arkansas with case managment, housing stability and crisis intervention.
His work also includes assisting veterans who become involved with the criminal justice system, it said. Scars and Stripes works with the Garland County District Court's Smart Justice Program to provide support and advocacy for veterans in the program.
The John Percifull Chapter will meet at the Garland County Library. Guests are welcome.
DAR membership is open to women who can document their lineage to an ancestor who supported the American cause during the Revolutionary War.
